newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks cut losses at close on bargain hunt.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks cut losses at close on bargain hunt.

text.p: Jakarta stocks closed 1.35 percent down but off their lows on Wednesday as bargain hunters quickly bought cheap stocks near the close, brokers said.
Active bargain hunting of some stocks belonging to the Lippo Group helped in the rebound after the market briefly fell more than two percent.
The Jakarta composite index ended down 9.36 points, or 1.35 percent, at 686.16 points after moving mostly in negative territory throughout the day.
In the broader market, losers led gainers by 114 to 31, with 44 issues unchanged. Total trading value was 558 billion rupiah on a total volume of 249.84 million shares.

"Players sold stocks almost across the board because of disappointment in 1996 earnings of key companies such as Sampoerna, but they bought back rapidly before the close," one broker with a foreign brokerage firm said.

Jakarta stocks were likely to stay weak on Thursday with reports of rises in the domestic inflation rate and fears of higher interest rates in the United States seen as further dampening sentiment, brokers said.

Indonesia's consumer price index rose 1.05 percent month-on-month in February, compared with 1.03 percent in January, Information Minister Harmoko said after the monthly economic cabinet meeting on Wednesday.
Another broker, however, said the current prices of some key stocks should provide buying opportunities as the overall outlook for 1997 corporate earnings was not that gloomy.
Harmoko also said Indonesia posted a trade surplus of $6.9 billion in 1996 against $4.75 billion in 1995. Total exports were $49.81 billion against imports of $42.87 billion.
Brokers said reports of the country's healthy trade surplus and expected encouraging earnings from other key stocks should prompt players to look for bargain issues.
Lippo Securities, Lippo Bank and Multipolar were among stocks that ended higher due to late bargain hunting, brokers said.
Cement stocks Semen Gresik, Semen Cibinong and Indocement were among the losers on continued talk that national cement supply was likely to exceed demand in 1998.
"There is likely to be an oversupply as some of the cement firms' new plants are expected to come on stream next year," one broker with a Hong Kong brokerage firm said.
Bank BNI, the day's most active stock, ended 50 rupiah lower at 1,600 rupiah, with some 29 million shares traded as some analysts said its 1996 results were lower than expected.
